beats.text: Bangladesh has 61% arable land. In the USA, it is 17%.
Bangladesh is the world's highest. This includes land under temporary crops, gardens, and temporary fallow, but excludes abandoned shifting cultivation.
Canada and Australia have just 4%. Huge countries, but very little is ready for the plow.
India has 52%. That is 3.1 times the share in the USA.
China has 12% and Japan has 11%. Both sit just above the global median of 10%.
Nigeria has 41%. A high share for a large nation, including fields left fallow.
The leaders? Bangladesh 61%, Denmark 59%, and The Gambia 58%.
